summary.short: Sets rules for certifying outbound transfers of personal information by Chinese personal information handlers through accredited certification bodies, with eligibility limits and an effective date of 1 January 2026.
summary.long: Issued by the CAC and SAMR (Order No. 20, 14 October 2025, adopted 21 July 2025), the measures govern transfers of personal information out of China through certification by a professional certification body. Eligible handlers must not be critical information infrastructure operators and must cumulatively transfer, from 1 January of a year, personal information (excluding sensitive personal information and important data) of 100,000 to under 1 million people, or sensitive personal information of under 10,000 people; splitting volumes to evade a security assessment is prohibited. Before applying, handlers must give notice, obtain separate consent where required and complete an impact assessment covering six listed factors. Certificates last three years, with renewal applications due six months before expiry. Certification bodies must file with the CAC, report certificate changes within five working days, and suspend or revoke certificates when transfers fall outside the certified scope. The CAC and SAMR set rules and standards, supervise certification, and may summon certified handlers facing significant risk. Overseas handlers must act through a domestic establishment or designated representative. The measures take effect on 1 January 2026.

obligations.summary: The National Cyberspace Administration, together with the national data management department and other relevant departments, formulates standards and technical specifications for outbound personal information certification.

evidence.quote: 国家网信部门会同国家数据管理部门和其他有关部门制定个人信息出境认证相关标准、技术规范

obligations.summary: A personal information processor providing personal information abroad through certification must simultaneously meet the listed conditions: not a critical information infrastructure operator, and cumulative outbound volume of 100,000 or more but fewer than 1 million individuals' personal information (excluding sensitive personal information), or fewer than 10,000 individuals' sensitive personal information, counted from 1 January of the current year. Important data is excluded.
obligations.conditional_on: Unless laws, administrative regulations or the national cyberspace authority provide otherwise

obligations.summary: A personal information processor may not use quantity-splitting or similar means to route personal information that must pass an outbound security assessment through the certification route.

obligations.summary: Before applying for certification for outbound provision, the processor must conduct a personal information protection impact assessment covering six listed matters (purpose and lawfulness, scale and sensitivity, overseas recipient's obligations and capabilities, risks after transfer, foreign legal environment, other matters).
